es: Seguir la reconstrucción de un viaje que cambió de planes e identificar qué se iba a hacer, qué cambió y cómo terminó.

teaching.en: Mia's brother was going to lend us his car, but on Friday he said he needed it.
teaching.es: El hermano de Mia iba a prestarnos su coche, pero el viernes dijo que lo necesitaba.
teaching.explanationEs: Was going to + lend: el plan original; but introduce el cambio.
segments: Mia's brother was going to lend us his car,
but on Friday he said he needed it.
teaching.audioText: Mia's brother was going to lend us his car, but on Friday he said he needed it.

teaching.en: We were about to cancel the trip when Carlos offered to take us by train.
teaching.es: Estábamos a punto de cancelar el viaje cuando Carlos se ofreció a llevarnos en tren.
teaching.explanationEs: Was about to + when + pasado simple: algo inminente y lo que lo interrumpe.
segments: We were about to cancel the trip when
Carlos offered to take us by train.
teaching.audioText: We were about to cancel the trip when Carlos offered to take us by train.

teaching.en: We thought the train would be quick, but it was delayed for two hours.
teaching.es: Pensamos que el tren sería rápido, pero se retrasó dos horas.
teaching.explanationEs: Would be: lo que esperábamos; was delayed: la realidad.
segments: We thought the train would be quick,
but it was delayed for two hours.
teaching.audioText: We thought the train would be quick, but it was delayed for two hours.

teaching.en: In the end, we reached the coast at noon and stayed until sunset.
teaching.es: Al final llegamos a la costa a mediodía y nos quedamos hasta la puesta de sol.
teaching.explanationEs: In the end introduce el resultado final en pasado simple.
segments: In the end, we reached the coast
at noon and stayed until sunset.
teaching.audioText: In the end, we reached the coast at noon and stayed until sunset.

teaching.en: The trip almost didn't happen, but it was a great day.
teaching.es: El viaje casi no ocurrió, pero fue un gran día.
teaching.explanationEs: Almost didn't + verbo: estuvo cerca de no ocurrir.

teaching.audioText: The trip almost didn't happen, but it was a great day.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál era el plan original del viaje?

choices.text: To go to the coast by car.
To go to the coast by train.
To cancel the trip on Friday.

feedback.es: El plan original era ir a la costa en coche; el tren fue el cambio y cancelar estuvo a punto de ocurrir.

hint.es: Es lo que se iba a hacer antes de que cambiara algo.

origin.text: We were going to go to the coast by car on Saturday. Mia's brother was going to lend us his car, but on Friday he said he needed it. We were about to cancel the trip when Carlos offered to take us by train instead. We thought the train would be quick, but it was delayed for two hours. In the end, we reached the coast at noon and stayed until sunset.

feedback.es: El viernes el hermano de Mia dijo que necesitaba el coche: por eso el plan cambió.

hint.es: Busca lo que ocurrió el viernes.

origin.audio: We were going to meet at the cinema, but Mia said she had a cold. We were about to cancel when Tom suggested watching the film at my house. In the end, we watched it there.

prompt.es: ¿Qué plan tenían Tom y Ana para el domingo?

choices.text: Having a picnic in the park.

feedback.es: Iban a hacer un picnic en el parque; habían comprado la comida el sábado, pero no era el plan en sí.

origin.text: Tom and Ana were going to have a picnic in the park on Sunday. They had bought the food on Saturday, but on Sunday morning it started to rain. They were about to give up when the sun came out at noon. They thought the park would be full of people, but it was almost empty. In the end, they had the best picnic of the summer.
